subject: git
claim: git switch and git restore, added in Git 2.23, split the two jobs of git checkout: switch changes branches and refuses to throw away local changes unless you pass --discard-changes, while restore brings back file contents from the index or from a commit without moving HEAD. Scripts that call git checkout with a path keep working, but the newer documentation teaches the two narrower commands first.

run.code:
git switch --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
git restore --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
echo ok

source.quote: THIS COMMAND IS EXPERIMENTAL. THE BEHAVIOR MAY CHANGE.
